summary: Simpson tower in Fairfield County, South Carolina: built with CCC labor in 1939-40, replaced by a steel structure in 1957-58; the register lists it as removed.

facts.design: steel structure (1957-58 replacement for an earlier wooden tower)
facts.status_note: Listed as removed. No source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: New tower built at the site under the CCC construction program; the report covers 7/1/39 to 6/30/40, so the exact year is not given
Old wooden tower replaced by a new steel structure; the report covers 7/1/57 to 6/30/58

evidence.supports: agency is the South Carolina Forestry Commission

evidence.quote: Report of the State Commission of Forestry, 7/1/39 to 6/30/40

evidence.supports: CCC did tower construction at no cost to the state
evidence.quote: All fire towers, tower buildings and telephone line construction was done by the Civilian Conservation Corps at no cost to the State or protective associations.

evidence.supports: new tower constructed at the Simpson site
evidence.quote: A new tower was constructed at the Simpson tower site in Fairfield County.

evidence.supports: CCC completed tower unit buildings at Simpson
evidence.quote: The C.C.C. completed tower unit buildings at the Simpson tower site and others.
Each tower unit contains the following buildings: a four room dwelling, barn, chicken house, smokehouse and latrine.

evidence.supports: tower sites about ten acres with a year-round house for the operator
evidence.quote: Most tower sites consisted of 10 acres of land, the tower, and a year-round dwelling for the operator.
Report of the State Commission of Forestry, 7/1/57 to 6/30/58

evidence.supports: old wooden tower replaced by steel structure
evidence.quote: The old wooden tower located at Simpson was replaced by a new steel structure.

evidence.supports: wooden towers statewide replaced by steel structures
evidence.quote: Eventually, all wooden towers were replaced by steel structures.

evidence.supports: most operators from the 1960s on were women
evidence.quote: From the 1960s on, most South Carolina tower operators were women
frequently their husbands were employed as firefighters

evidence.supports: state fire tower system closed 1 October 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

notes_for_editor: The register quotes the state commission's annual reports rather than reproducing them; the primary reports were not seen. The register gives 'Removed' with no date, so no removal event is recorded. The 1939 year is the start of the report period (7/1/39 to 6/30/40), so it is approximate. The 1957-58 report says the replaced tower was 'old wooden'; the sources do not say whether the 1939-40 tower was that wooden tower, and the story does not say so. The record's coordinates (OSM node) and the existing weebly photo were not re-checked.
